title: T811-906GS GROUND-BASED IMAGING SYSTEM FOR ATTITUDE DETERMINATION AND IN-ORBIT SERVICING SUPPORT OF LEO OBJECTS (EXPRO+)
description: Current technologies for retrieving attitude information of a space object are based on radar imaging, passive optical light curves or laser ranges. Radar technologies operate independently of weather conditions but require prior information about the observed target. Laser-based technologies need a target equipped with retroreflector and light curves are limited by the target angular velocity on the sky and its attitude. The slow tumbling rate of a LEO satellite, combined with the brief duration of its pass, limits the amount of data available for accurate attitude reconstruction.  Although weather-dependent, imaging technology provides a high-resolution snapshot of the observed object, showing - without prior information or additional processing - whether the target is intact and how it is oriented in space. A series of images combined with a simple model of the target will allow to accurately estimate its rotational state providing a full description of its attitude. The attitude determination will be demonstrated using simulated data.  The imaging technology can support several aspects of the space safety, it will enhance the sensitivity and the astrometric accuracy of the observation system allowing the detection of fainter objects supporting both planetary defense and space debris population model refinement. Finally, the use of direct imaging technology for the characterization of re-entry events should be evaluated.

title: ERS-EO NEW PRODUCT DEVELOPMENTS: AGENTIC AI FOR EO IN PPDR - EXPRO+
description: As part of the European Resilience from Space - Earth Observation (ERS-EO) Programme Element 2, this tender covers the development and demonstration of new Earth Observation (EO)-based products supported by agentic artificial intelligence for Public Protection and Disaster Relief (PPDR). Each contract will have a maximum value of 2 million and an expected duration of 24 months.The activities will develop suites of new EO-based products adapted to the needs of PPDR users. The products will use satellite imagery as a primary input and combine it with complementary data sources. They will be benchmarked against existing solutions to demonstrate improvements in areas such as accuracy, timeliness, coverage and ease of use.Each activity will also develop an agentic AI engine supporting the discovery, integration, benchmarking and recommendation of EO products and data. The developed capabilities will include reusable interfaces and a user workspace with an AI copilot and will be demonstrated with representative PPDR users. Product operationalisation is outside the scope of the activities.The Agency intends to select up to four (4) proposals, to be implemented through separate contracts. Each proposal shall address at least one of the following PPDR user groups and may address more than one:(1) Civil protection and emergency management;(2) Law enforcement;(3) Fire and rescue; and(4) Border and coast guard.In selecting the overall portfolio, the Agency will seek broad and complementary coverage of these PPDR user groups. The complementarity of proposals and the avoidance of unnecessary duplication between the user communities addressed may therefore be taken into account in the selection.This tender is addressed to economic operators from countries participating in ERS-EO Programme Element 2. The placement and distribution of contracts will be subject to the availability of funding under the applicable national programme subscriptions.The key tasks and outputs are expected to include:(1) Definition of PPDR use cases, requirements and fitness-for-use criteria;(2) Development and benchmarking of new EO-based products combining satellite imagery with complementary data;(3) Development of an agentic AI engine, reusable interfaces and a user workspace;(4) Verification, validation, security and assurance activities;(5) Demonstration and evaluation with representative PPDR users; and(6) Preparation of a roadmap for possible future integration into Space Resilience Node environments.

title: LARGE ANGLE FLEXURE PIVOT WITH INTEGRATED CONSTANT TORQUE MECHANISM -EXPRO+
description: Objective: To incorporate Constant Torque Mechanisms into Large Angle Flexure Pivot mechanisms in order to reduce driving torque requirements and power needed to operate the mechanism and maximise angular motion range of flexible pivot with Constant Torque Mechanism.Description: This activity aims to integrate Large Angle Flexure Pivot (LAFP) mechanisms with innovative Constant Torque Mechanisms (CTMs) to reduce the torque/force required for actuation. Previous developments on flexural pivots have demonstrated their suitability for high-precision and lubrication-free applications; however, actuation remains a limiting factor for large-angle movements. This activity focuses on addressing this limitation through the use of CTMs. The development of a dedicated actuator is explicitly excluded from the scope. The combination of CTMs with LAFPs provides a promising alternative to traditional rigid-body hinges and standalone compliant pivots. This hybrid approach aims to maintain the benefits of compliant mechanismssuch as zero backlash and inter-element gaps, high precision, absence of lubrication, and reduced wear debris due to elastic deformationwhile reducing actuation effort. These properties are particularly relevant for long-duration space missions and fine-pointing applications, where high-precision and reliability are critical. The integration of CTMs is expected to improve the stability of the flexures while reducing actuation force (and power needed to operate them), making them more competitive and suitable for long-term space missions. Additionally, a key innovation under consideration is a dual-mode functionality, enabling the mechanism to switch between a compliant mode and a stiff configuration. This feature would allow the mechanism to remain locked during launch and operate flexibly in orbit. The flexible pivot with an integrated Constant Torque Mechanism would find application in high-stability pointing mechanisms for optical payloads and pointing mechanisms. The key benefits include reduced actuation torque (and power requirements) and the potential implementation of bi-stable stiffness, which could be adjusted to secure compliant components during launch. This would be added value on top of other benefits of using compliant mechanisms for pointing applications such as lack of lubrication, reduced contamination and precise motion etc. The tasks foreseen in this activity include: - Concept definition and literature review. Assess existing CTM designs and develop initial concepts for large angle flex pivot with integrated CTM. - Breadboard design of the integrated CTM-Flexure mechanism. - Breadboard manufacturing of Large Angle Flexure Pivot with Integrated Constant Torque Mechanism - Characterisation and functional testing to validate torque reduction and stiffness adjustment capabilities. title: REACTION CONTROL SYSTEM THRUSTER FED WITH GASES FROM CRYOGENIC PROPELLANTS - EXPRO+
description: Objective: To develop a breadboard of a reaction control system thruster, fed with gaseous methane or hydrogen and gaseous oxygen, as part of a unified propulsion system with a main engine fed by LOX/LH2/LCH4.Description: In the last decade, alternative propellants for space exploration have become a tangible reality, with more and more companies investing in new propellant combinations. Currently, some of the most promising propellant combinations include Oxygen, Hydrogen and Methane. These propellants show potential to be used for gaseous fed reaction control system (RCS) thrusters. RCS thrusters enable attitude control or main thrust capability for small spacecrafts, without the use of a separate propulsion system. This activity tests the new propellant combinations in RCS thrusters. Such thruster could enable higher performance than storable propellants. As well, Oxygen, Methane and Hydrogen can be sourced or produced on other planets (ISRU, e.g. Mars, Moon) which could enable new exploration mission scenarios. This development designs and preliminary tests an RCS thruster that is fed by gaseous oxygen as oxydiser and either gaseous methane or gaseous hydrogen asfuel. The thrusters requirements shall be in line with selected use cases of exploration missions (e.g. lunar lander or interplanetary vehicle). This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Perform a trade-off on propellant selection (considering i.e. GOX/GH2or GOX/GCH4), thrust of the main thruster, and scaled up and down version for preliminary study (i.e. 100N - 500N). - Perform preliminary design, investigating pulsed operation (and necessary ignition technology) - Design, manufacture and test a breadboard model of an RCS thruster, including functional tests - Perform a preliminary study on thrust scalability
